name: InfoBento
description: Solar-powered color eInk decorator for kitchen counters, desks, and shelves. Single front-mounted color eInk display in a monolithic white housing with a thin bezel; solar panel on the upper portion of the back side; no hinge, no MagSafe, no kickstand — the body is the stand. Designed to survive a 4-foot drop. Configure once on a web page; refreshes once or twice a day on solar power for months. $30-40 target via Kickstarter. (Pivoted 2026-04-22 from a previous dual-display MagSafe clamshell concept — see Round 10 note.)

artifacts.name: Device Owner
artifacts.description: Individual who owns an InfoBento display and places it on a counter, shelf, or windowsill in their home or office
responsibilities: Configure bento boxes via web UI
Place device on a counter or shelf with the solar panel exposed to indirect window light
Complete first-time Wi-Fi (or phone) pairing during setup
Update configuration occasionally as priorities change

artifacts.name: Gifter
artifacts.description: Person who purchases and pre-configures an InfoBento as a gift for someone else
responsibilities: Configure initial bento layout for recipient
Pair device to recipients phone or hand off config

artifacts.name: Daily Glancer
artifacts.description: Busy professional who wants a calm passive display of key daily info — weather, next event, a quote — visible at a glance from across the room. The founder is this user. (Demoted to secondary 2026-04-22 in the counter-only pivot — original primary scenario was a phone-mounted display, which has been removed.)
goals: See today's weather and schedule without picking up a phone
Reduce screen time by offloading ambient info to a passive display
Customize what info matters most to them
frustrations: Checking phone for simple info leads to distraction rabbit holes
Smart home displays are too expensive and power-hungry
Existing e-paper gadgets are not customizable
Every phone interaction is an attention trap — even a quick weather check becomes 10 minutes of scrolling

artifacts.name: Desk Decorator
artifacts.description: Person who values aesthetic, minimal desk or counter accessories and wants a small display that shows a rotating quote, countdown to vacation, or personal QR code — standing on its own with the solar panel as kickstand
goals: Have a visually pleasing desk or counter accessory that is also functional
Display a personal link or QR code for networking
A device that charges itself near a window without any cables
frustrations: Digital photo frames are too large and power-hungry
Sticky notes with countdowns look unprofessional
No small, elegant way to display a personal QR code
Desk gadgets always need cables or batteries

artifacts.name: Gift Giver
artifacts.description: Someone who wants to give a thoughtful, personalized tech gift that is useful without being overwhelming
goals: Give a unique gift that feels personal and curated
Pre-configure the device so the recipient can use it immediately
Gift something that does not require technical knowledge to enjoy
frustrations: Most tech gifts require complex setup
Subscription-based gifts feel like an obligation

artifacts.name: Zero Device Interaction
artifacts.statement: The InfoBento itself requires no interaction — no buttons, no app to open, no charging ritual. You interact with your phone; InfoBento is just there.
artifacts.description: InfoBento has no user-facing controls. It syncs automatically via BLE, charges via solar or MagSafe passively, and refreshes on schedule. The user's only interaction is glancing at it — either on the back of their phone or standing on a counter. Configuration happens once via web UI.
artifacts.source: Core product vision — reduce screen time, not add to it. Refined in round 4: zero interaction with the device, not zero interaction period.
examples: Flip phone over to glance at display — no unlock needed
Auto-sync via BLE when mounted on phone
Solar charging when standing on counter near window
Passive MagSafe charging when collapsed on phone
No buttons anywhere on the device
counterExamples: Dedicated companion app that must be opened

artifacts.name: Pure Function Architecture
artifacts.statement: The API must be stateless — same config in, same frame buffer out, every time
artifacts.description: No server-side state, no user accounts for MVP, no databases. The cloud API is a pure function that takes a BentoConfig and returns rendered frame data. Config lives on the client (localStorage + phone).
artifacts.source: Technical constraint — edge deployability, power budget, simplicity
examples: POST /api/render takes config JSON, returns binary frame
Config stored in browser localStorage
Phone caches last frame for offline use

artifacts.name: Limited-Palette Elegance
artifacts.statement: Design for the constraint — a small color palette should feel intentional, not limited
artifacts.description: The color eInk display has a fixed ~7-color palette (Spectra 6 / ACeP family). Rather than fighting this constraint, embrace it. Whitespace-driven hierarchy, two font sizes (hero Spleen 8x16 + data 5x7), color used as accent and category cue rather than gradient or detail. Think e-paper signage, screen-printed posters, and risograph aesthetics — dense but legible. Color is a noun (this is the temperature, this is the date, this is a warning), never a verb.
artifacts.source: Hardware constraint + design research (round 6) + counter-pivot color decision (round 10). Replaces the prior 1-Bit Elegance principle when the panel moved from monochrome to 7-color.
examples: Hero font for primary data, drawn in red for hot temps and blue for cold
Thin horizontal rules as section dividers (not box borders)
Whitespace gaps between sections instead of 1px borders
Color used as category cue: weather in red/blue, calendar in muted gray, countdown number in red
QR codes stay black-only (color QR doesn't scan reliably)
counterExamples: Anti-aliased fonts that become muddy at low color depth
Using all 7 colors in a single box (creates noise)
More than two font sizes (creates visual noise)

artifacts.name: Free by Default
artifacts.statement: MVP box types must work without accounts, API keys, or subscriptions
artifacts.description: The five MVP box types (weather, quote, countdown, QR, text) all use free data sources or local computation. No user should need to create an account anywhere to use the basic product.
artifacts.source: User research — friction in setup kills adoption for consumer hardware
examples: Weather via Open-Meteo (no API key)
Quotes via ZenQuotes (no auth)
Countdown and QR are pure local computation
Text is user-entered
counterExamples: Requiring Google Calendar OAuth for MVP
Paid weather API with key management
Mandatory account creation before first use

artifacts.label: REQ-001
artifacts.statement: User can configure 3-6 bento boxes on the eInk display via web interface
artifacts.source: Voice spec — user wants modular customizable information boxes
artifacts.rationale: Core product value proposition — modular, personalized information display

artifacts.label: REQ-002
artifacts.statement: Device syncs display data through paired phone via BLE without requiring WiFi
artifacts.source: Voice spec — device should not be dependent on specific WiFi SSID
artifacts.rationale: Portability is key — device travels with user on phone back or in pocket, phone bridges connectivity

artifacts.label: REQ-003
artifacts.statement: Display refreshes 1-2 times per day on solar power alone under normal indoor lighting (counter-standing mode). Phone-mounted mode refreshes every few minutes via MagSafe charging.
artifacts.source: Voice spec + hardware research (issue #22). AEM10941 solar IC harvests 5-15mAh/day at 200 lux, device needs ~1mAh/day in counter mode.
artifacts.rationale: Zero-maintenance power — user should never need to charge the device manually. Dual power modes match the two physical modes.

artifacts.label: REQ-004
artifacts.statement: MVP supports 5 box types without requiring any user accounts: weather, quote, countdown, QR, text
artifacts.source: Open question resolution — free data sources prioritized for MVP
artifacts.rationale: Reduces onboarding friction to zero — unbox, configure, done

artifacts.label: REQ-005
artifacts.statement: Web UI and API served from same port in production with full HMR in development
artifacts.source: Open question resolution — same-port architecture like phasebot, Hono framework
artifacts.rationale: Simplifies deployment (single process) and dev experience (Vite HMR + API proxy)

artifacts.label: REQ-006
artifacts.statement: Config persists in browser localStorage with JSON export/import for portability
artifacts.source: Open question resolution — no server-side state for MVP
artifacts.rationale: Avoids auth complexity while keeping config portable between devices

artifacts.name: Morning glance at kitchen counter
artifacts.setting: Kitchen counter near window, 7:15 AM, making coffee before commute
artifacts.narrative: Sam's InfoBento is standing on the kitchen counter, hinged open at ~100 degrees with the solar panel aimed at the window. The P display (inner, facing the room) shows a relaxed layout: weather (62F, partly cloudy), a countdown (14 days to vacation), and a motivational quote. Sam grabs a jacket based on the weather. Before heading out, they fold the InfoBento closed and snap it onto the back of their phone via MagSafe. The D display (outer) was already showing a dense real-time layout: time, next meeting, message counts. No re-render needed — D held its frame from the last BLE sync. Total interaction with the device: zero.
preconditions: Config has weather, countdown, and quote boxes
Phone was in BLE range at scheduled refresh time
InfoBento was standing on counter near window overnight (solar charging)
postconditions: User has ambient awareness of weather and upcoming event without touching any device
Device transitions from counter mode to phone-mounted mode for the commute

artifacts.name: First-time web configuration
artifacts.setting: Home office, laptop open, just unboxed the InfoBento device
artifacts.narrative: Alex opens infobento.com on their laptop. The web UI shows a 128x296 eInk preview on the left with D (Phone) and P (Counter) toggle tabs. They configure D first: add Weather (type Portland), add Countdown (anniversary date), add Text (personal motto). The live preview updates after each change in sharp 1-bit black and white. They switch to P and add a Quote box and a relaxed weather layout. They click Export Config and save the JSON to pair with the phone app later.
postconditions: User has a saved BentoConfig with 3 boxes
Config is in localStorage and optionally exported as JSON

artifacts.name: Gifting a pre-configured device
artifacts.setting: Living room, wrapping gifts for a friends birthday
artifacts.narrative: Jordan buys an InfoBento for their friend who loves hiking. They open the web UI and configure 3 boxes: weather for the friends city, a countdown to their next planned hike, and a QR code linking to their shared trail playlist. Jordan exports the config as JSON and includes a card with pairing instructions. The friend opens the gift, pairs it with their phone in under a minute, and the display shows Jordans curated layout.
preconditions: Config is exportable as JSON file
postconditions: Recipient has a working device with a personalized config they did not have to create themselves

artifacts.name: Single Color eInk Layout
artifacts.description: Single color eInk panel on the front of the counter device. Calm, multi-section layout optimized for at-a-glance reading from across a room. 7-color palette (Spectra 6 / ACeP family). Final panel resolution chosen in #35.
elements: 3-6 sections — quote, full weather, countdown hero, agenda, QR, text — depending on panel size
Spleen 8x16 hero font for primary data, 5x7 data font for labels and body
Thin horizontal rules as section dividers
Color used as category cue: weather temps in red/blue, countdown number in red, qr in black, body text in black
Multi-column layouts viable on larger panels (5.65" / 7.3")
annotations: 7-color palette — palette-indexed framebuffer, 3 bits per pixel
Color as accent and category, not gradient or photographic detail
Refresh once or twice a day on solar power (~15-30s per refresh on color panels)
Frame buffer size derived from chosen panel via frameBufferBytes() helper in @infobento/core
Layout limit (currently MAX_BOXES=6) revisits after panel selection — larger color panels comfortably support 8-10 boxes

artifacts.name: Web Configuration Editor
artifacts.description: Main web UI screen where users configure their counter device's bento boxes. Vanilla JS with reactive state pattern. Client-side renderer for instant preview. Currently ships a dual-display 2x2 layout (clamshell-era), being collapsed to a single column in #29.
elements: Top: live color eInk preview rendered client-side, sized 1:1 with the device
Below: box list with up/down arrow buttons for reordering
Header: Menu dropdown with Import / Export JSON
Per-cell: Add Box button with type picker dropdown
Per-box config form (location for weather/forecast, date+label for countdown, URL for QR, textarea for text, text+author for quote)
Consent dialog (Privacy + Terms) on first load, persisted in localStorage
annotations: Preview renders client-side using @infobento/renderer — no API round-trip
Single-display editor (post #29 collapse). Until #29 lands, dual-display 2x2 layout is still shipping.
No account required — config lives in localStorage with JSON import/export
Responsive layout: stacks vertically on narrow viewports (<=720px)
Vanilla JS with reactive state, no framework
All 6 box types supported: text, countdown, weather, 3hr forecast, qr, quote
Geocoding via Nominatim handles 'Portland, OR', addresses, and landmarks like 'Mt. St. Helens'

artifacts.title: Open Question Decisions — Rounds 1-5
artifacts.body:
Decisions made during planning sessions:

## Round 1 (resolved)
- MVP box types: weather (Open-Meteo), quote (ZenQuotes), countdown, QR, text — all free, no auth
- Web framework: Hono + Vite (same-port architecture like phasebot)
- Web app private during dev, co-hosted with tiles- and webmap.dev later
- Version starts at 0.1.0

## Round 2 (resolved)
1. MVP scope: text + countdown + weather first (proves pipeline), then QR + quote
2. Weather location: Open-Meteo geocoding API, user types city name
3. Config persistence: localStorage + JSON export/import (no server state)
4. Refresh scheduling: web UI sets schedule, phone app executes it, device responds
5. Design language: clean/minimal with sharp borders, receipt-style typography
6. Name: InfoBento (confirmed final)

## Round 3 (resolved)
1. Implementation order: text -> countdown -> weather -> QR -> quote
2. Mobile web layout: stack vertically (preview on top, config below)
3. Font: embedded small fixed-width bitmap font (5x7 or 6x8 pixel, embedded-systems style)
4. QR sizing: larger allocation — half display height or more, not constrained to a thin box
5. Name confirmed: InfoBento is final

## Round 4 — Market & Positioning (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Primary user: Daily Glancer (the founder)
2. Distribution: Kickstarter
3. Price target: $30 (bumped from $25 after BOM analysis)
4. Hardware: ESP32-C3 + eInk + battery w/ solar drip charger + solar panel kickstand (details in issue #22)
5. Competitive positioning: resolved — 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' anti-phone angle

## Round 5 — Form Factor & Interaction Model (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Form factor: clamshell with 180-degree hinge. Two halves: eInk display + solar panel
2. Primary mode: MagSafe-mounted on back of iPhone, eInk facing out. User flips phone to peek.
3. Secondary mode: standing on counter/desk, hinge open, solar panel aimed at window, display facing room
4. Size constraint: must fit on iPhone 15 Pro back (146.6 x 70.6mm), may partially cover camera
6. Interaction model: zero interaction with InfoBento itself. No buttons, no app to open.
7. Refresh rate: must increase in phone-mounted mode (minutes, not hours) vs standalone (1-2x/day)
8. MVP stays simple (weather, countdown, text, QR, quote). Authenticated integrations (calendar, messages, smart home) come post-MVP.
9. Kitchen counter is the hero Kickstarter scenario. Phone-mounted is the daily use case.

## Round 6 — Phase Scoping (resolved 2026-04-21)

### Phase 2 (core) — COMPLETE
1. Zod validation with field-level error paths (validateBentoConfig)
2. Each box renderer handles its own data fetching/parsing
3. Horizontal subdivision (split: 'left' | 'right') implemented
4. Display resolution: 128x296 portrait, abstracted via constants

### Phase 3 (renderer) — COMPLETE
1. All 5 box renderers with hero font + whitespace layout + icons
2. Spleen 8x16 hero font + 5x7 data font + 7x7 icon set
3. CUT: dithering (no grayscale sources), frame diffing (no firmware yet)
4. Renderer stays pure — API fetching handled by web/api packages

### Phase 4 (API) — COMPLETE
1. Structured error responses via Zod validation with field-level paths
2. frameToPng re-exported from api package
3. Health endpoint reads version from package.json dynamically
4. Box-types endpoint lists only 5 implemented types
5. /api/quote proxy for ZenQuotes (bypasses CORS)

### Phase 5 (web) — COMPLETE
1. Vanilla JS with reactive state, D/P display toggle
2. Client-side 1-bit canvas renderer, localStorage, import/export JSON
3. Live weather fetch (Open-Meteo), random quote (/api/quote proxy)
4. Mobile responsive CSS, empty states, input validation
5. 1-bit icon set in box headers
6. Deployed to infobento.com (nginx + systemd)

## Still open (hardware)
- Hinge sourcing: Reell TI-C5M selected, need to order samples
- Background BLE on iOS constraints (critical for phone-mounted mode)
- eInk partial refresh strategy for D display (minute-level updates)
- BLE connection interval tuning for phone-mounted mode
- BOM at $30: dual display pushes total range to $29-50, aggressive sourcing critical

## Resolved (no longer open)
- BLE version: 5.0 (ESP32-C3 supports it natively)
- Battery capacity: ~100mAh target (352035 form factor)
- Anti-aliasing: not possible at 1-bit, solved with purpose-designed Spleen 8x16 font
- Hinge: 180-degree standard friction, book-style along 70.6mm short edge (reduced from 320-degree)
- MagSafe: full N52 ring on solar half (M-side), Qi coil inside ring
- Price: $30
- Thickness: ~8mm folded (accepted)
- Display panel: glass (not flex)
- Display resolution: 128x296 portrait
- Battery placement: solar half — avoids grip flex stress on LiPo cell. Power through hinge FPC (2 wires, ~100mA). Display half has no battery.
- Folded thickness: ~7.2mm (3.2mm display + 4.0mm solar) (standard 2.9-inch panel rotated). Codebase updated.
- Physical modes: closed (0° phone-mounted), peek (90°), counter (~100° solar charging)
- Solar charging: counter mode only, not phone-mounted

## Round 7 — Hardware Design Decisions (resolved 2026-04-21)
1. Glass eInk panel (not flex) — flex adds $7-10/unit for 0.9mm savings, not worth it at this stage
2. Accept ~8mm folded thickness — position as 'slim enough for a back pocket' (comparable to MagSafe Battery Pack at 11.3mm, thinner than most phone cases with card holders)
3. Price target bumped from $25 to $30 — BOM analysis showed charging subsystem ($13-18) + hinge ($4-30) + display ($5-8) leaves no margin at $25
4. See issue #22 for full hardware design exploration and proposed component layout

## Round 8 — Physical Modes & Hinge Hardening (2026-04-21)

### Four-surface labeling
The device has 2 halves x 2 sides = 4 distinct surfaces:
- D = eInk display (outer face of display half) — phone-mounted content
- P = eInk display (inner face of display half) — counter/peek content
- S = Solar panel (inner face of solar half)
- M = MagSafe + Qi (outer face of solar half — magnets, coil)
When closed: D faces out, M faces phone, P and S sandwiched inside.

### Three operating modes (180-degree hinge)
1. CLOSED (0°) — Phone mounted. M touches phone (MagSafe holds), D faces outward. Display visible on phone back. Solar not charging.
2. PEEK (90°) — Quick glance. Solar half flat, display half vertical. L-shape. User opens device 90° to read display while phone is on desk.
3. COUNTER (~100°) — Solar charging. M-side down as base, S faces up toward light, D faces user at angle. Standalone on counter/desk.

### Decisions
1. Peek mode is 90° (not 10-20° as originally discussed) — clear L-shape, display fully visible
2. Counter mode: solar half is the base (M-side down), solar panel faces up for charging
3. Simultaneous mount+stand is NOT a use case — device is either on phone or on counter
4. Solar charging only happens in counter mode (not phone-mounted)
5. FLAT (180°) exists mechanically but is not a useful operating mode — storage/transport only

### Dual display — DECIDED: yes, same size (Variant A)
- Two 2.9-inch 128x296 eInk panels back-to-back on display half PCB
- D (outer): real-time phone-mounted content, partial refresh every 2-5 min
- P (inner): ambient counter/peek content, full refresh 1-2x/day
- GPIO budget: 10 of 13 pins, 3 spare. Shared SPI + RST.
- Thickness: 3.2mm display half (improved from 4.4mm single-display)
- BOM: +$5-8 for second panel
- No re-render on mode switch — each display holds its own frame
- Software: extend BentoConfig with displayId: 'D' | 'P', two independent configs
- Display resolution confirmed: 128x296 portrait. Codebase updated.

artifacts.label: REQ-007
artifacts.statement: QR code box type gets a larger vertical allocation (approximately half display height) to ensure scannability
artifacts.source: Open question resolution — small QR codes in thin boxes are not scannable
artifacts.rationale: A QR code in a 35px-tall box would be too small to scan reliably. Larger allocation ensures real-world utility.

artifacts.name: Two-Font Bitmap System
artifacts.statement: Two embedded bitmap fonts — Spleen 8x16 for hero data, built-in 5x7 for labels and body text — no system font dependencies
artifacts.description: The renderer embeds two fixed-width bitmap fonts as pixel data arrays. Spleen 8x16 (purpose-designed, MIT licensed) for hero numbers and primary data (temperatures, times, countdown numbers). Built-in 5x7 for labels, secondary text, and compact data rows. Two sizes only — the contrast jump IS the visual hierarchy. No medium size.
artifacts.source: Font comparison (round 6) — Spleen 8x16 selected over Tamzen 8x16, Tamzen 10x20, and 2x-scaled 5x7 baseline. Best curve quality at minimal vertical cost.
examples: Built-in 5x7: 'WEATHER', 'Partly Cloudy', 'H:68 L:55'
Two sizes create clear hierarchy without borders
counterExamples: System fonts rendered via Canvas API
Three or more font sizes (creates visual noise)

artifacts.name: Rendering Pipeline (v0.4.0+)
artifacts.description: Full rendering pipeline: BentoConfig (with displayId D|P, Zod-validated) -> layout (vertical + horizontal split) -> hero font (Spleen 8x16) + icons + whitespace -> draw -> 4736-byte frame buffer. All 5 MVP box types. Deployed to infobento.com.
artifacts.scope: Core types with Zod validation, layout engine (128x296, horizontal split), dual fonts, icons, 5 box renderers, web editor with D/P toggle + canvas + localStorage, API with structured errors, deployed
knownLimitations: No center alignment in text rendering
Maximum 6 boxes enforced by layout truncation
Weather and quote data fetched client-side only (no server-side caching)
No phone app or firmware yet — software demo only

artifacts.title: Type system allowed box type / config mismatch
artifacts.description: Original BentoBox interface used a single optional BoxConfig field, allowing { type: weather, config: { type: text } } without type error. Fixed with discriminated union (TextBentoBox | UnconfiguredBentoBox).
artifacts.evidence: Claude code review round 2, item #4 — TypeScript accepted mismatched type/config pairs
artifacts.recommendation: Maintain discriminated union pattern as new box types are added. Each box type gets its own interface pairing type with config.

artifacts.label: REQ-008
artifacts.statement: Users can see a live PNG preview of their bento layout before syncing to device
artifacts.source: Implementation need — raw binary frame buffer is not human-viewable; preview is essential for the web config experience
artifacts.rationale: Users cannot configure a display they cannot see. The first-time config scenario depends on immediate visual feedback. Phone app also needs preview before BLE sync.

artifacts.name: Solar-Powered Counter Display
artifacts.statement: InfoBento is a monolithic counter device — single color eInk display on the front, solar panel on the upper portion of the back, body-as-stand. No hinge, no MagSafe, no kickstand.
artifacts.description: The device is a single white-housed body with a thin bezel (≤4mm visible). Front: color eInk panel recessed into the bezel rim so the rim shields the glass on a face-down drop. Back-upper: solar panel cavity (~70x100mm) for indirect window-light harvesting. Back-lower: ESP32 + battery + grip area. The back surface tilts ~12-15° relative to the front so the device naturally angles its display upward when set on a flat counter — no separate kickstand needed. Designed to survive a 4-foot drop via a soft polymer bumper layer between glass and housing, edge-radiused corners, and the inset display recess. Refreshes once or twice a day on solar power; counter-only, no phone-mounted mode.
artifacts.source: Round 10 counter pivot (2026-04-22). Replaces the prior dual-display MagSafe clamshell concept after user-class fit analysis showed the clamshell was trying to serve two products at once and paying for it with BOM, thickness, and the iOS background BLE risk.
examples: Kitchen counter: device leans slightly back on its own footprint, display angled toward standing viewer, solar panel catching window light from the upper back surface
Desk: device sits next to a monitor, calm color quote and weather visible from working distance
Shelf: device functions as ambient decor — quote, countdown, weather — no plug, no cable
Dropped onto hardwood from 4 feet: bumper compresses, edges absorb impact, glass intact
counterExamples: Wall-mounted display (mounting hardware adds friction; counter placement is the hero)

artifacts.title: Hardware Platform
artifacts.body:
## Counter device platform (rewritten 2026-04-22 for the counter-only color pivot)

Monolithic single-body counter device. White housing, thin bezel, no hinge, no MagSafe, no kickstand. Final dimensions and panel SKU pending #35.

### Front
- Single color eInk panel (Spectra 6 / ACeP family, 7-color palette)
- Panel SKU candidates (pending #35):
  - Good Display 4.2" Spectra 6 (640x400, 7 colors, $20-28)
  - Pervasive 5.65" ACeP (600x448, 7 colors, $30-40)
  - Good Display 7.3" Spectra 6 (800x480, 7 colors, $40-55)
- Bezel: ≤4mm visible on all four sides
- Display recess: deep enough that the bezel rim shields the glass on a face-down drop

### Back-upper
- Solar panel cavity, ~70x100mm amorphous-Si, 0.22mm thick
- Mounted on the upper third of the back surface so it catches indirect window light when the device sits on a counter
- AEM10941 solar harvesting IC drives charging

### Back-lower
- ESP32-C3 (BLE-only) or ESP32-C6 (Wi-Fi 6 + BLE) — chosen in #35
- LiPo battery: ~100mAh target (may bump to 150-200mAh after color-refresh power profile finalized)
- MCP73831 LiPo charger
- Provides grip area when device is picked up

### Industrial design
- White housing (color locked, founder decision)
- Edge-radiused corners (~4mm radius) to disperse impact energy
- Back surface tilts ~12-15° relative to front so device naturally angles its display upward when placed on a flat counter — body-as-stand, no separate kickstand mechanism
- Soft polymer bumper layer between the eInk glass and the housing rim (silicone vs TPU vs over-molded TPE — choice pending)
- Designed to survive a 4-foot drop onto a hard surface (drop-test protocol in #36 / `docs/hardware/DROP-TEST.md`)

### Connectivity (decision in #35)
- Wi-Fi direct (likely): ESP32-C6, fetches frames from cloud API directly. Removes the iOS background-BLE risk that gated the previous concept. First-time setup via captive portal.
- Phone-bridged BLE (fallback): ESP32-C3, phone app fetches and pushes via BLE. Lower per-refresh power but adds a phone-app dependency.

### GPIO allocation (preliminary, single-display)
- SPI: MOSI, SCLK, CS, DC, BUSY, RST for the single panel — 6 pins
- Battery ADC: 1 pin
- Wi-Fi/BLE: handled by MCU module
- Plenty of GPIO headroom (was tight at 10/13 with dual-display; now ~7 used)

### Thickness
- Estimated 8-12mm depending on chosen panel and battery — single body, no fold
- Less aggressive than the prior 7.2mm folded clamshell, but the device is decorator-class (sits on a counter), not pocket-class — thickness is not a hero spec

### BOM target: $30-40 retail
- Color eInk panel: $20-55 (the variable; biggest BOM line)
- ESP32-C3 or C6: $2-4
- LiPo battery + AEM10941 + MCP73831: $5-7
- Solar panel: $2-4
- Housing (injection-molded white plastic at volume): $3-6
- Bumper (silicone or TPU): $1-2
- Assembly + packaging: $3-5
- Subtotal range: ~$36-83. Mid-range targets ($30-40 retail) require choosing the smaller panel (4.2") and aggressive sourcing.

### What's gone vs the clamshell concept
- Second eInk panel and its driver lines
- Hinge, hinge FPC, hinge sourcing risk
- MagSafe N52 magnet ring and Qi receiver IC (STWLC38 / BQ51013)
- iOS background BLE as a project risk
- Dual-PCB / through-hinge power routing
- Reell TI-C5M hinge sample order

artifacts.title: Market & Distribution
artifacts.body:
## Positioning (rewritten 2026-04-22 for the counter-only color pivot)
- Price target: $30-40 retail (final number gated on panel choice in #35)
- Distribution: Kickstarter
- Timeline: when the prototype hardware exists and the color renderer ships (Phases 3 + 4)
- Primary buyer: Desk Decorator and Gift Giver. Daily Glancer is now secondary (the phone-mounted story is gone).

## Competitive landscape
- Phone widgets / lock screen: free, but still require pick-up + wake. Not a counter object.
- Smartwatch complications: on wrist, small, subscription-heavy. Different surface entirely.
- Tidbyt / Vestaboard / LaMetric: $150-300, monochrome dot-matrix or LED, Wi-Fi dependent, desk-only. InfoBento beats them on price, color depth, and zero subscriptions.
- DIY eInk frames (Waveshare, LILYGO, Inkplate): $25-80 unassembled, no polish, requires coding. InfoBento is the assembled, polished version.
- Digital photo frames: $40-200, color, but require power cables and have no contextual content.

## InfoBento's gap
- Cheaper than smart displays, color where they're monochrome
- More polished than DIY eInk, no coding required
- Solar-powered, no cable, no plug
- No accounts, no subscriptions, no Wi-Fi dependency (depending on connectivity choice in #35)
- The calm decorator: ambient information without the pull of a phone screen

## Kickstarter hero scenario
- Kitchen counter, morning light, color quote and weather visible from across the room while the user makes coffee. Solar panel on the upper back surface catches the window.

## Value proposition — counter-only revision 2026-04-22
- Tagline: See what matters. Skip the spiral.
- Angle: a calm color decorator for your counter. The information you check most often, sitting there in soft color eInk, on its own, on sunlight.
- Price justification: less than a smart display, more polished than DIY, color where the alternatives are monochrome.
- Structural moat vs Tidbyt: color, no Wi-Fi setup ritual (if Wi-Fi-direct is captive-portal style), no monthly fee, ten times cheaper.
- Resolved tension: it's a 'small calm surface for the room' — not a gadget, not a smart-home device.

## Kickstarter pitch (counter-only revision 2026-04-22)
Most of the time, your phone holds your whole life beautifully. But sometimes you just want to know if it's going to rain, or how many days until your trip, without opening five apps and resurfacing twenty minutes later. InfoBento is a small color eInk decorator that sits on your counter, your desk, or a shelf. Weather, your next meeting, the countdown you're looking forward to, a quote that lifts the room — all visible at a glance from across the room, in soft color eInk on a thin white frame. The body is its own stand. The solar panel on the upper back catches indirect light through the window. No Wi-Fi setup ritual, no account to make, no batteries to swap, no buttons to press. Configure your boxes once on a web page and it just works — for months, silently, on sunlight. At $30-40, InfoBento isn't a smart home device or a screen competing for your attention. It's a small calm surface for the room — what matters, where it matters, and nothing else.

## Alternate angles (kept for reference)
- Angle 2: A photo frame that knows what to show. Conveys the calm-decorator framing well, but undersells the customization.
- Angle 3: The opposite of a smart display. Defines by contrast — risky if backers don't already have the smart-display reference point.

artifacts.title: Display resolution mismatch: code vs hardware (fixed in v0.4.0)
artifacts.description: The codebase originally used 240x200 (placeholder). Standard 2.9-inch eInk panels are 296x128. Fixed: codebase now uses 128x296 portrait orientation (panel rotated 90°). All tests, renderers, and preview scripts updated.

artifacts.title: eInk display design research — layout patterns (addressed)
artifacts.description:
Research across Tidbyt, Watchy, TRMNL, thermal printer art, and eInk phone accessories (YotaPhone, InkCase, HiSense) yielded consistent design principles for small 1-bit displays:

1. ONE DOMINANT ELEMENT — a single large hero element (time, temperature) taking 40-50% of height reads best. Cramming too much kills legibility.
2. TWO FONT SIZES MAX — large hero + small data. No medium. The contrast jump IS the hierarchy.
3. WHITESPACE BEATS BORDERS — generous padding between sections feels cleaner than 1px borders around everything. Current renderer over-uses borders.
4. RECEIPT-STYLE LAYOUT — label left-aligned, value right-aligned, monospace. Horizontal rules as dividers.
5. 3-4 DATA ITEMS MAX — rotate screens for more info rather than crowding one frame.
6. STATIC > INTERACTIVE — eInk phone accessories that tried to be mini-Android (YotaPhone, HiSense) disappointed users. Single-purpose static frames (InkCase clock faces) worked best.
7. NO TOUCH REQUIRED — designs assuming eInk touch input universally failed. Treat the back as display-only.

The current renderer treats all boxes identically (border + uppercase label + dotted divider + wrapped text). The research points toward differentiated visual treatment per box type as the next rendering improvement.
artifacts.evidence: Web research: Tidbyt review (macwright.com), Watchy docs (sqfmi), TRMNL (trmnl.com), YotaPhone review (Engadget, Phone Scoop), InkCase (Kickstarter), thermal-sans-mono (GitHub)
artifacts.recommendation: Implement hero font size for primary data (weather temp, countdown number). Reduce border usage — use whitespace gaps instead. Differentiate box renderers visually by type. Consider screen rotation (2-3 states cycling) as an alternative to cramming 6 boxes.

artifacts.title: Round 9 — Editor v0.5 polish (2026-04-22)
artifacts.body:
Web editor changes that landed this session, in support of the demo's role as the Kickstarter campaign's interactive proof point.

## Layout — dual-display always visible
- Replaced the `D (Phone)` / `P (Counter)` toggle with a 2x2 CSS grid: previews on top (Outer left, Inner right), editors below in the same alignment.
- 'Outer' / 'Inner' labels (was `D` / `P`) make the public-vs-private mental model explicit at a glance.
- Header chrome cleaned up: title `InfoBento`, `EDITOR vX.Y.Z` badge with version stamped from package.json at build time, single right-aligned `Menu` dropdown for Import / Export JSON.
- Mobile (≤720px) stacks all four panels vertically: Outer Preview, Inner Preview, Outer Editor, Inner Editor.
- Live preview was clipping to the top ~22% of the layout because `#eink-display` was hard-sized to 240×200 with overflow:hidden while the canvas painted at 384×888 (CSS legacy from before the canvas approach). Resolved by sizing the panel from the canvas via CSS variables (`--eink-w` / `--eink-h`) published by the renderer.

## Geocoding — Nominatim (OpenStreetMap)
- Weather and 3hr Forecast boxes now resolve free-form locations via Nominatim instead of Open-Meteo's geocoder.
- Open-Meteo couldn't handle 'Portland, OR' (no admin filter) or landmarks like 'Mt. St. Helens'. Nominatim handles both naturally — addresses, towns, regions, peaks.
- Open-Meteo still serves the actual weather/hourly data; only geocoding moved.

## New box type — 3hr Forecast
- Editor type with the same UX as Weather: location field, auto-fetch on mount, status string under the input.
- Renders as three rows of `time | tempF | condition` from Open-Meteo's hourly endpoint, slicing the next 3 hours from current.
- Adds a 6th MVP box type (was 5: text, countdown, weather, qr, quote). Updates REQ-004 implicitly — 6 box types now.

## Consent dialog
- First-load modal covering both Privacy and Terms, single Accept button, persisted in localStorage with a CONSENT_VERSION integer so future material policy changes can re-prompt.
- Content grounded in 'Free by Default' and 'Pure Function Architecture' principles: no accounts, no tracking, no telemetry, third-party calls (Open-Meteo / Nominatim / ZenQuotes) named explicitly. Tagline 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' as subtitle.

## Display dimensions — corrected to spec
- Codebase had been shipping 128×296 (the panel-native portrait orientation). Project documentation and CLAUDE.md called for 240×200 (landscape, after rotation). Constants updated to 240×200.
- Tests refactored to derive frame buffer size and dimensions from `DISPLAY_WIDTH` / `DISPLAY_HEIGHT` / `DEFAULT_FRAME_BYTES` instead of hard-coded literals (4736, 128, 296). Future spec change is now a one-line edit in `constants.ts`.
- Hardware notes elsewhere in this project.json still say `128x296 portrait` in several places (Hardware Platform note, dual-display section of Round 8). Code-vs-doc mismatch to resolve as a follow-up before campaign launch.

## Tagline + pitch tone (revised 2026-04-22)
- Tagline changed from 'See less. Know enough.' to 'See what matters. Skip the spiral.' Same anti-distraction intent, gentler framing.
- Kickstarter pitch (angle 1) revised to lead with what users gain rather than what they fear. Drops 'anti-phone', 'trapdoor', 'screen time saved' framing in favor of 'a calm companion to your phone' angle. Closing line now: 'It's a small, calm surface that lets you skip the spiral when all you needed was a glance.'
- Daily Glancer / Desk Decorator user-class frustrations left as-is — those are authentic user pain points, not marketing voice.

## Misc fixes
- Vite `pngjs` browser stub now uses an actual file (`packages/web/src/stubs/pngjs.ts`) instead of `/dev/null`, so vite build works on Windows (`/dev/null` resolved to `C:\dev\null` and broke).
- Web bundle reads version from package.json at build time via Vite's `define: { __APP_VERSION__: ... }`. Every release auto-stamps the badge.
- Eink display preview SCALE = 1, panel sizes itself to the canvas via CSS vars — bumping SCALE to enlarge the preview is a one-line change.
- Empty-state message in preview canvas: `<Add a box...>` (replaces 'Add a box to see your display').

## Quality gate (committed clean)
- `npm run build` (tsc): pass
- `npm test` (vitest): 74/74 pass
- `npm run lint` (eslint): pass
- `npm run format:check` (prettier): pass
- `vite build`: pass on Windows and Linux

artifacts.title: Campaign Phase Plan
artifacts.body:
Project advances from `demo-polish` to `campaign` as of 2026-04-22. Significantly revised by the Round 10 counter pivot — open hardware list shrank dramatically, color renderer added to open eng list.

## Goal
Convert the working web editor + working hardware prototype into a funded Kickstarter campaign for the counter-only color decorator.

## Phase entry criteria (met)
- All six MVP box types implemented (text, countdown, weather, 3hr forecast, qr, quote)
- Web editor deployed and demo-polished (consent dialog, robust geocoding, version stamping)
- Pitch and value-prop revised for the counter-only color story (see `Market & Distribution` note)
- Project artifacts coherent for the counter device after the Round 10 pivot

## Phase exit criteria
- Kickstarter campaign live
- Funding target hit (or campaign concluded with decision on next move)
- Backers have a realistic delivery date and clear communication channel

## Open deliverables
- **Kickstarter project page** — long-form pitch in `Market & Distribution` note is the source text; needs page-formatted version with sections, images, FAQs (#38).
- **Pitch video** — 60-90s. Needs script, storyboard, talent (founder) (#38).
- **Hero photography + product video** — requires working prototype on a counter in window light.
- **Working hardware prototype** — gating: panel + MCU choice (#35), SCAD rewrite + 3D-print (#34), drop test (#36).
- **Reward tiers + pricing** — $30-40 unit price target (final after panel pick); backer reward structure TBD (early-bird, retail, multi-pack, gift bundle).
- **Stretch goals** — TBD. Candidates: extra box types (calendar, transit), additional housing colors beyond white, accessory bundles, larger panel SKU as upgrade tier.
- **Pre-launch landing page + email signup** — Kickstarter `Follow` button before campaign open. Co-host on infobento.com.
- **Press kit** — one-pager + photos + spec sheet for outlets and reviewers.

## Open engineering items (pivot-related)
- **Color renderer (Phase 3, #33)** — color framebuffer + draw primitives (#30), color box renderers + PNG (#31), web preview color paint (#32). Largest engineering lift; on a feature branch.
- **Collapse dual-display (Phase 2, #29)** — mechanical refactor; gates Phase 3.
- **Wi-Fi setup UX** — captive portal vs alternatives (decision in #35).

## Open questions for the campaign
- Campaign duration (30 vs 45 days)
- Funding target — covers tooling + first batch + Kickstarter+payment fees (~10%) + shipping shortfall buffer
- Manufacturing partner (PCB house + injection-molded white housing + assembly + packaging)
- Shipping plan — US + international? Add-on fulfillment partner?
- Refund / cancellation policy
- Late-pledge / BackerKit strategy

## Open hardware items (post-pivot)
- Panel SKU + MCU decision (#35) — gates renderer dimensions
- SCAD rewrite for monolithic body (#34) — drop-resistant industrial design
- Drop-test protocol + run (#36)
- Bumper material decision (silicone vs TPU vs over-molded TPE)

## Items removed by the pivot (no longer gating)
- ~~Hinge sourcing (Reell TI-C5M)~~ — no hinge
- ~~iOS background BLE spike~~ — Wi-Fi-direct kills this risk
- ~~eInk partial refresh strategy for D display~~ — no minute-level mode
- ~~BLE connection interval tuning for phone-mounted mode~~ — no phone-mounted mode
- ~~Display dimensions reconciliation (128x296 vs 240x200)~~ — both irrelevant; new color panel sets new dimensions in #35

## Demo as marketing lever
- The web editor at infobento.com is the campaign's interactive credibility lever ('try it now in your browser before you back it'). Keep the editor polished and bug-free for the duration of the campaign.
- Once the color renderer ships (Phase 3), the editor's preview becomes a much more compelling visual.
- Each new box type added during the campaign is a campaign update opportunity.

## Next concrete moves (founder action)

2. Decide panel SKU + MCU + connectivity model (#35) — gates Phase 3a (#30) and SCAD work (#34)

artifacts.title: Round 10 — Counter Pivot (2026-04-22)
artifacts.body:
## What
InfoBento pivots from a dual-display MagSafe clamshell to a single counter-only color eInk decorator. Phone-back use case is gone. MagSafe, hinge, dual-display PCB, kickstand, and the iOS background BLE risk are all removed. Color eInk replaces 1-bit. Solar panel moves to the upper portion of the back side of a monolithic body. Industrial design constrained to white housing, ≤4mm bezel, drop-resistant to 4 feet.

## Why
The user-class fit analysis revealed the clamshell was trying to serve two products at once and paying for it: ~$30 BOM, ~7.2mm thickness, GPIO pressure, hinge sourcing risk, and (most critically) iOS background BLE as a single point of failure that could not be answered before manufacturing capital was committed. The counter device — previously the secondary mode — turns out to be the more de-risked, photogenic, giftable, and Kickstartable product on what we already know. Daily Glancer (the founder) was the user class that justified phone-back; Desk Decorator and Gift Giver are better served by counter-only and were second-class citizens in the dual-display story.

The color upgrade and panel upsize were chosen to differentiate the counter device from monochrome competitors (Tidbyt, generic eInk frames) and to make Kickstarter photography visually striking.

## Decisions made in this round
- Hard pivot: phone-back is gone, not deferred to v2
- Color eInk panel (Spectra 6 or ACeP family, 7-color)
- Larger panel size to be picked from 4.2" / 5.65" / 7.3" candidates in #35
- Drop the kickstand: monolithic body with ~12-15° back-tilt, body-as-stand
- Solar panel mounted on upper portion of back side
- White housing, thin bezel (≤4mm)
- Designed for 4-foot drop survival (bumper layer, edge radius, recessed display)

## Decisions still pending (gate Phase 2+)
- Final panel SKU (#35)
- MCU choice: ESP32-C3 vs C6 (#35)
- Connectivity model: Wi-Fi direct vs phone-bridged BLE (#35)
- Bumper material: silicone vs TPU vs over-molded TPE
- Final battery capacity (color refresh + Wi-Fi may push past 100mAh)
- Wi-Fi setup UX (captive portal leading)

## What changes (tracked in pivot/counter-color milestone)
GitHub issues #25-#38 break this pivot into phases:
- #25 — Pivot RFC (this decision record)
- #28 + subs (#26, #27) — strategic artifacts (project.json, README, docs) — IN PROGRESS
- #29 — collapse dual-display in code
- #33 + subs (#30, #31, #32) — color-aware renderer
- #37 + subs (#34, #35, #36) — hardware (SCAD, panel sourcing, drop test)
- #38 — campaign rewrite

## What stays
- @infobento/core types (BentoBox, BentoConfig, layout engine)
- @infobento/api (Hono, validation, /api/quote, /api/health)
- All 6 box types (text, countdown, weather, qr, quote, 3hr forecast)
- Nominatim geocoding, Open-Meteo, ZenQuotes
- Consent dialog, localStorage + JSON import/export
- Web editor (with the dual-display 2x2 layout collapsed in #29)
- Design principles: Pure Function Architecture, Free by Default, Zero Device Interaction, Two-Font Bitmap System
- currentPhase stays 'campaign' — the pivot reshapes the campaign, doesn't reset the phase

## What's deleted from this project.json
- Scenario 'Phone-back peek before unlock'
- Wireframe 'Dual eInk Display Layout' (replaced with 'Single Color eInk Layout')
- Design principle 'MagSafe Dual-Display Clamshell' (replaced with 'Solar-Powered Counter Display')
- Design principle '1-Bit Elegance' (replaced with 'Limited-Palette Elegance')
- Daily Glancer demoted from primary
